newsitem.title: USA: TWA to reorganize JFK operations - pilots.
newsitem.headline: TWA to reorganize JFK operations - pilots.

text.p: Trans World Airlines Inc plans to reorganize its operations at JFK International Airport and reduce peak summer flying hours, the pilots union said Monday.
TWA will present its 1997 operating plan at a regular board meeting Tuesday, the union said.
The airline seeks to "reorganize operations at JFK into a more profitable flying plan internationally," the Air Line Pilots Association at TWA said.
The plan also calls for a "small reduction" in peak summer flying hours, the union said.

TWA recently announced some winter service cutbacks, primarily at New York's JFK airport. Under the winter plan, TWA will make "significant" reductions in Boeing 747 operations during the first quarter but will increase its Boeing 767 and 757 flying, the union said.
The board also may announce the selection of a new chief executive officer at Tuesday's meeting, the union said.

Jonathan Ornstein, chief executive of low-cost European carrier Virgin Express, a Virgin Group member, was reported to be a top contender for the job. But Ornstein told Reuters he was not seeking a job at St. Louis-based TWA.

The airline is searching for a successor to Jeffrey Erickson, who will leave the company January. Erickson's 2-1/2-year reign included the company's bankruptcy reorganization and the aftermath of the fatal Flight 800 crash in July.
TWA did not immediately return calls seeking comment.
